description: Execution-grounded benchmark and repair corpus targets for complex functional Amiga code generation.

benchmark_families.title: MOD Player Controls With Stateful Playback
benchmark_families.first_shot_prompt: Generate Amiga 68k assembly for a tracker module control panel with Play and Stop buttons, Paula channel 0 playback state, and clean left mouse exit.
structured_model_requirements: Declare controls for play and stop with stable ids and visible labels.
Declare Paula hardware dependency and playback state variables.
Declare action routines for PlayMOD and StopMOD.
runtime_evidence: AUD0LC, AUD0LEN, AUD0PER, and AUD0VOL writes are present.
DMACON enables and stops audio DMA.
PlaybackState is set and cleared by action routines.
Boot-time PlayMOD preview makes Paula registers observable without synthetic mouse input.
multi_turn_follow_ups: add a Volume Up button without changing Play or Stop
add Pause and Mute buttons, keeping the existing controls
rename Stop to Halt and move Volume Up below Play
set the initial volume to 48 and the volume step to 4
change playback note to A-3 and keep all controls
rejected_turns: add another Volume Up button with the same identity
rename the third button without enough buttons
set volume step to louder
make the Play button both stop and mute

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Remove the DMACON audio enable write from PlayMOD.
repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore the Paula DMA enable write without changing controls or labels.

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Drop the existing Stop control while applying a Volume Up follow-up.
repair_seeds.target_repair: Reinsert the preserved Stop control and dispatch path.

verified_follow_ups: add a third button called Volume Up
add a fourth button called Volume Down
verified_rejected_turns: add another Volume Up button with the same identity
set volume step to louder
rename the third button without enough buttons
make the Play button both stop and mute

benchmark_families.title: Double-Buffered Bitplane Animation With Sprite/Copper Interaction
benchmark_families.first_shot_prompt: Generate double-buffered bitplane animation that swaps front red and back green bitplane pointers on vblank, overlays a small sprite, updates a copper color register, and exits on left mouse click.
structured_model_requirements: Declare front and back buffer state with editable colors.
Declare WaitVBlank and buffer-swap routines.
Declare bitplane, sprite, copper, and CIA hardware plus visible frame data labels.
runtime_evidence: Front and back COLOR01 writes are present.
BPL1PT is written for both front and back buffers.
WaitVBlank paces the pointer swap.
An owned copper list refreshes BPLCON0, BPL1PT, SPR0PT, and palette registers.
Sprite pointer evidence is present for the interaction layer.
multi_turn_follow_ups: change the front buffer to blue and the back buffer to yellow
make the sprite move downward while keeping the buffer swap
slow the animation by waiting two vblanks
change the copper accent color to purple
rejected_turns: set the front color to invisible
make both buffers use the same pointer
remove vblank pacing
turn it into HAM mode without changing anything else

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Replace one BPL1PT write with a duplicate of the other buffer pointer.
repair_seeds.expected_diagnostic: missing BPL1PT writes for both front/back buffers
repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore distinct front and back BPL1PT writes paced by WaitVBlank.

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Delete one visible frame data label.
repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore the missing buffer pattern data without changing color state.

verified_follow_ups: set front color to red and back color to blue
verified_rejected_turns: set front color to teal
set front color to
set front color to greenhouse
set back color to
set front color to red and back color

benchmark_families.title: Blitter Object Movement With Bounds And Collision
benchmark_families.first_shot_prompt: Generate an Amiga 68k blitter BOB demo that moves a masked object inside screen bounds, detects collision with a rectangular target, changes color on collision, and exits on left mouse.
structured_model_requirements: Declare BOB position, velocity, bounds, and collision target state.
Declare blitter copy, mask, wait, and collision routines.
Declare bitplane and blitter hardware dependencies.
runtime_evidence: BLTCON0/BLTCON1, BLTAPT/BLTBPT/BLTCPT/BLTDPT, and BLTSIZE writes are present.
Canonical DMACONR blitter wait is present before and after BLTSIZE.
Position state changes are bounded before blit start.
Collision state drives a visible COLOR register change.

verified_follow_ups: make the object move faster horizontally
move the collision rectangle to the right side
verified_rejected_turns: start the blitter without waiting
move outside the screen bounds
use a negative blit size
remove the mask but keep masked collision

multi_turn_follow_ups: make the object move faster horizontally
move the collision rectangle to the right side
change collision color to blue
add keyboard or joystick direction control while preserving mouse exit
rejected_turns: start the blitter without waiting
move outside the screen bounds
use a negative blit size
remove the mask but keep masked collision

repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore the post-start blitter wait without changing object state.

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Let X position increment without right-edge clamp.
repair_seeds.target_repair: Clamp or bounce X position before programming blitter pointers.

benchmark_families.title: Copper List Effects With Runtime Raster Validation
benchmark_families.first_shot_prompt: Generate an Amiga 68k copper list demo with bouncing raster bars, frame-counted color cycling, and clean left mouse exit.
structured_model_requirements: Declare copper list pointer setup and color table state.
Declare frame counter and raster bar position state.
Declare copper, vblank, and input hardware dependencies.
runtime_evidence: COP1LC/COPJMP1 writes install the copper list.
Copper WAIT and COLOR words create multiple raster bands.
Vblank-paced state updates rewrite copper WAIT positions across frames.
Expected frame validation samples non-black colored horizontal bands.
multi_turn_follow_ups: increase the number of bars to eight
make the bars bounce slower
change the palette to blue and white
add a top status band without losing the animation
rejected_turns: create a copper wait past the end of display
use an odd copper instruction address
remove the copper jump but keep animation
set zero bars

repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore copper start without changing list data.

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Make all copper color words black.
repair_seeds.expected_diagnostic: runtime frame lacks expected colored raster bands
repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore distinct visible colors in the copper list.

verified_rejected_turns: create a copper wait past the end of display
use an odd copper instruction address
remove the copper jump but keep animation
set zero bars

benchmark_families.title: Mouse-Controlled Sprite With Multiplexing
benchmark_families.first_shot_prompt: Generate an Amiga 68k demo with a mouse-controlled sprite and a second multiplexed sprite copy that follows with an offset, exiting on left mouse.
structured_model_requirements: Declare sprite pointer data and mouse position state.
Declare multiplex offset state and sprite update routine.
Declare sprite, input, vblank, copper, and bitplane display hardware dependencies.
runtime_evidence: SPR0PTH/SPR0PTL and at least one additional sprite pointer write are present.
JOY0DAT or mouse/CIAA reads update position state.
Sprite control words are rewritten during vblank.
Bitplane DMA and a visible backdrop bitplane are active behind the sprites.
Expected frame validation finds visible sprite-colored pixels away from the border.
multi_turn_follow_ups: change the follower offset to 32 pixels
make the sprite green
add horizontal wrapping
make the follower lag by one frame
rejected_turns: write sprite pointers outside chip memory
make the sprite height zero
remove vblank update timing
use joystick movement while keeping mouse-only wording

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Remove the second sprite pointer write.
repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore the second sprite pointer and preserve mouse control.

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Move sprite control-word updates outside the vblank path.
repair_seeds.expected_diagnostic: sprite update not paced by vblank
repair_seeds.target_repair: Move sprite updates back under WaitVBlank.

verified_rejected_turns: write sprite pointers outside chip memory
make the sprite height zero
remove the second sprite but keep multiplexing
update sprites outside vblank

benchmark_families.title: Intuition Windowed Tool With Clean Resource Handling
benchmark_families.first_shot_prompt: Generate an AmigaOS-friendly 68k assembly program that opens intuition.library, creates a window with two gadgets, handles close events, and releases every resource cleanly.
structured_model_requirements: Declare library open/close state and window pointer state.
Declare event loop, gadget dispatch, and cleanup routines.
Declare Intuition, Exec, and DOS dependencies without custom-chip takeover.
runtime_evidence: OpenLibrary and CloseLibrary LVO calls are balanced.
OpenWindow and CloseWindow calls are balanced.
IDCMP close-window handling exits the event loop.
Failure paths release resources allocated before the failure.
multi_turn_follow_ups: add a third gadget called Volume Up
rename the Stop gadget to Halt
move the buttons to the bottom of the window
add a status text field without changing cleanup
rejected_turns: skip closing the window
open intuition twice but close it once
add a gadget with no bounds
handle close events by jumping into data

repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore cleanup on normal and failure exits.

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Return from close event without CloseWindow.
repair_seeds.target_repair: Close the window before library shutdown.

benchmark_families.title: Clean Takeover Demo With System Restore
benchmark_families.first_shot_prompt: Generate an Amiga 68k clean takeover demo that saves DMA, interrupt, view, copper, and palette state, runs a color-cycling hardware effect, and restores the system on left mouse exit.
structured_model_requirements: Declare saved DMA, interrupt, view, copper, and palette state.
Declare takeover, effect loop, and restore routines.
Declare custom chip, graphics library, input, and cleanup dependencies.
runtime_evidence: Original DMACON/INTENA/COP1LC state is saved before modification.
DMA and interrupt state are restored on every exit path.
LoadView or equivalent view restoration is present when the view is changed.
Palette/COLOR registers are restored or explicitly normalized before exit.
multi_turn_follow_ups: change the cycling palette to green tones
add a copper split while preserving restore
slow the effect to every other vblank
add a right mouse emergency restore path
rejected_turns: disable interrupts without restoring them
skip saving the old copper pointer
exit directly with RTS from the effect loop
overwrite saved DMA state with zero

repair_seeds.target_repair: Restore DMA state from the saved variable before exit.

repair_seeds.broken_variant_strategy: Add a right mouse exit that bypasses RestoreSystem.
repair_seeds.target_repair: Route every exit path through RestoreSystem.

verified_follow_ups: change the cycling palette to green tones
add a copper split while preserving restore
slow the effect to every other vblank
add a right mouse emergency restore path
verified_rejected_turns: disable interrupts without restoring them
skip saving the old copper pointer
exit directly with RTS from the effect loop
overwrite saved DMA state with zero
